This framework supports both engineering design decisions, such as tuning ranges, protection interactions, and control-mode transitions, and system-level assessment of stability, weak-grid behavior, and inverter-interaction modes. The Task 3 deliverables serve as the technical foundation for future commissioning and for any subsequent field demonstration of GFM capabilities at the Wheatridge hybrid plant or similar large-scale renewable facilities. 7.4 Task 4 – Community Benefits Plan and Workforce Development Task 4 focuses on laying the groundwork for workforce development and community benefits activities that are directly aligned with grid-forming (GFM) technology deployment. During BP1, the project team concentrated on curriculum and internship planning rather than executing a full-scale program, with the goal of ensuring that later phases would be able to integrate students into meaningful technical work related to inverter-based resources and hybrid-plant operation. Work under this task established a structured internship framework designed to provide hands-on experience in system planning and simulation, and hybrid-plant control analysis. The framework defines task-oriented learning modules, mentoring plans, and clear technical engagement pathways so that interns can contribute to ongoing modeling, positive-sequence studies, and analysis of inverter-based resource behavior. The design explicitly targets student participation from diverse backgrounds and emphasizes skill-building in power system modeling, renewable integration studies, and the use of advanced simulation tools. These planning activities produced two primary outcomes. First, the project defined an internship plan that specifies scope, objectives, technical activities, and expected skill development for participants. Second, the team developed a framework for incorporating students into active engineering tasks, including modeling, simulation, and analysis of IBR behavior, in a way that is technically meaningful and aligned with project needs. Together, these deliverables ensure that future workforce participants will have a clear pathway to engage with advanced GFM technologies using tools and workflows that are already in place. By the end of BP1, internship planning and technical learning modules were completed and positioned for use in later stages of the project. Direct implementation activities, such as involving students in field testing, advanced modeling campaigns, or on-site measurement analysis, were scheduled for subsequent phases and had not yet begun within the BP1 period of performance. 7.5 Task 5 - Project Management Page 16 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric Task 5 provided the project-management structure necessary to coordinate technical activities, maintain schedule discipline, and ensure the quality and completeness of all Budget Period 1 (BP1) deliverables.
